title: Can I BEAT Martin with NO Pieces?
summary: 'Beat Martin with NO pieces' is a trick title: he selects chess.com's 'blindfold pieces' setting so his board shows no pieces at all, then plays a normal full game vs Martin (250) from memory (viewers see the real game on the big board, his view on a mini board, plus an eval bar). He plays the London vs Martin's weird Dutch, remembers the position by patterns/relationships, wins material with knight forks and mates; game review rates his play ~1400 strength, Martin 70% accuracy.
rules: Normal chess, standard start, full armies for both sides.
Blindfold display: all pieces invisible on the player's board (chess.com 'blindfold pieces' piece set).

opponent.name: Martin
opponent.avatar_description: Cartoon bearded man with bushy eyebrows and a sweater; remake original.

board.theme_notes: chess.com brown board; player's board empty, viewer board shows pieces; eval bar at side.

visual_fx: Invisible pieces on the main board; small reference board optional.
